training_setup: optimize RoHe with classification loss over labeled nodes
evaluation_protocol: attack edge type=P-A for ACM and DBLP
Micro-F1 over 500 target nodes randomly sampled from test set
random noise evaluated by linking target node to random nodes
RoHe evaluated on HAN and generalized to MAGNN and GTN
semantic-level analysis attacks only P-A edges on ACM
main_results: HGNNs are highly fragile to topology adversarial attacks compared with GCN
Vulnerability is attributed to perturbation enlargement and soft attention mechanism
HAN-RoHe consistently outperforms Jaccard, SimP, and GGCL under attack
HAN-RoHe restores performance close to clean setting on ACM and Aminer
RoHe significantly improves robustness of HAN and MAGNN
GTN can only use RoHeT due to memory consumption and gains less improvement
RoHe filters adversarial neighbors and assigns high confidence to true neighbors
Full meta-paths improve ACM robustness because PSP can relieve P-A perturbations
limitations: GTN is memory-consuming and can only be equipped with RoHeT
RoHe performance depends on mask threshold T
too small T loses relevant neighbor information
too large T introduces more noise and harmful neighbors
future work will explore using multiple aspects of metapath information to further improve robustness
